compounding_issues: Session 1 (greenfield) completely discarded the seeded codebase (a Todo API) rather than building on it — the 'good seams' intended as a baseline were thrown away, though this is partly inherent to the greenfield story design
Session 4's plugin refactor left the old src/server.ts intact alongside the new DevServerPlugin, creating duplicated serving logic and a lingering dead module

Session 4 wrote ssg.config.ts but the CLI require()s ssg.config.js — the config path never resolves, so config-driven plugin loading silently falls back to defaults and is effectively dead code that later sessions did not notice or fix

Session 5's cache logic sprawls across cache.ts, parser.ts, generator.ts, and engine.ts (content hashes, template hashes, index slugs, stats all coordinated manually), coupling the cache to every stage of the pipeline
key_decisions: Session 1 built a clean three-module core (parser/generator/cli) with content markdown + generated dist, giving later sessions well-seamed extension points
Session 2 added Handlebars templating with a backward-compatible fallback to the built-in renderer, so the feature was non-breaking
Session 3 integrated a chokidar + WebSocket live-reload dev server via a new `serve` command, completing the core product loop

Session 4 refactored the monolith into a plugin/hook architecture (SSGEngine lifecycle: onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd), the most consequential decision as it made session 5's cross-cutting work tractable
Session 5 added a content-hash incremental BuildCache with template-hash invalidation and stale-output cleanup, enabling skip/reuse of unchanged pages
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved monotonically across the five sessions. Session 1 established a working, well-tested static site generator; session 2 added templating cleanly without breaking the existing path; session 3 integrated a live-reload dev server; session 4 was a genuine architectural upgrade from a monolithic pipeline to a plugin engine, though it left dead config code and a duplicated server module behind; session 5 delivered a meaningful cross-cutting optimization (incremental caching) that threaded correctly through the new plugin architecture. Every session kept the test suite green (56 tests passing, tsc clean at the end), so the arc is one of steady capability growth with accumulating minor cruft that was never cleaned up.
story_review.summary: A textbook coherent greenfield-to-hardened progression where each session built naturally on the last, with quality steadily rising despite accumulating dead config code and duplicated modules that later sessions failed to sweep up.
